context: Initially, root 4 has left child 3 and right child 5. Node 3 has only left child 1, and 1 has only left child 0. Nodes 0 and 5 are leaves.

The balance factor is the height of the left subtree minus the height of the right. Height is measured in edges: a leaf has height 0 and an empty subtree has height −1. Checking from the bottom up, the first unbalanced node is 3, labeled node. Its left child, 1, is labeled child.
description: Here the right subtree of child (1) is empty. The code first saves grand_child = child.right, then sets child.right = node and finally node.left = grand_child. Save the old reference before overwriting it.

frames.announcement: Check balance factors from the bottom up to find the first unbalanced node, 3.
frames.explanation: Initially, root 4 has left child 3 and right child 5. Node 3 has only left child 1, and 1 has only left child 0. Nodes 0 and 5 are leaves. The balance factors shown below the nodes are 0 for nodes 0 and 5, 1 for node 1, and 2 for nodes 3 and 4. Moving up the left branch, the first unbalanced node is 3, so repair the subtree rooted at 3 first.
frames.key_state: Initially, root 4 has left child 3 and right child 5. Node 3 has left child 1, and 1 has left child 0. Both 3 and 4 have balance factor 2. Working upward, handle 3 first.
frames.title: Find the first unbalanced node, 3

frames.announcement: Mark the unbalanced subtree root, node = 3, and its left child, child = 1.
frames.explanation: Mark node=3 and child=1. Before rotation, root 4 still has left child 3 and right child 5. Node 3 has only left child 1, and 1 has only left child 0. Since child.right is empty, the saved grand_child is empty, and node.left should be empty after rotation.
frames.key_state: Before rotation, root 4 has left child 3 and right child 5, node 3 has left child 1, and 1 has left child 0. Here node=3, child=1, and child.right is empty.
frames.title: Mark the two nodes for rotation

frames.announcement: Node 3 becomes the right child of 1. The local subtree has formed and awaits reconnection to parent 4.
frames.explanation: Save the original right reference of child, which is empty. Then set child.right = node and node.left = grand_child to form the local subtree: root 1 has left child 0 and right child 3, both leaves. Parent 4 currently has only right child 5 in the figure. It has yet to connect to the new root 1. The dashed circle at the old position of 3 and its dashed edge to 1 show the old arrangement for comparison. That edge is no longer a connection, and the rotation is not yet complete.
frames.key_state: Local root 1 has left child 0 and right child 3. Parent 4 currently has only right child 5 and has yet to connect to new root 1.
frames.title: Form the local subtree rooted at 1

frames.announcement: Set parent 4's left pointer to new root 1. This completes the right rotation and restores balance throughout the tree.
frames.explanation: Point 4.left to new subtree root 1 to reconnect it. Root 4 now has left child 1 and right child 5. Node 1 has left child 0 and right child 3. Nodes 0, 3, and 5 are leaves. The local subtree height drops by 1, and root 4's balance factor drops from 2 to 1. The inorder sequence of the entire tree remains [0, 1, 3, 4, 5].
frames.key_state: After reconnection, root 4 has left child 1 and right child 5, and 1 has left child 0 and right child 3. The inorder sequence is [0, 1, 3, 4, 5], and the entire tree is balanced.
frames.title: Reconnect the new subtree root to its parent

result: The local subtree's height decreases by 1, restoring AVL balance throughout the tree and preserving the binary search tree ordering.
summary: Rotate the first unbalanced node to the right. Update the parent-child pointers within the subtree first, then reconnect its new root to the parent above it.
title: Right rotation in an AVL tree
